criteria.criterion: A new unit test in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs builds a reading with a boundary word in its summary and in an assumption, and `check_reading_acceptance` returns Ok; `cargo test -p athena-core` passes.
criteria.evidence: I ran the test and it passed. It puts the word in the summary and in assumptions[0], then unwraps `check_reading_acceptance` with the repo-file list set to None and to Some(files). It also asserts that `check_reading_text` returns Accept. Under the old all-fields scan the unwrap would panic, because the summary was refused. I also ran the end-to-end twin `run_pin_tests::a_reading_with_a_boundary_word_in_its_summary_is_accepted`, which passed. The full suite passed in the recorded CI run.

criteria.criterion: A unit test shows a reading whose deliverable path holds a boundary word is still refused with the path and word named, and a reading with a `content` acceptance criterion holding a boundary word is still refused naming `acceptance_criteria`; `cargo test -p athena-core` passes.
criteria.evidence: I ran both commands and both passed. For both the word and the fragment, the unit test asserts that `unwrap_err` names the path and the word for `docs/<term>.md`. It asserts that a content criterion is refused with `acceptance_criteria[0]` and the term named, and that the replay path refuses it too. The end-to-end test `a_reading_with_a_boundary_word_is_not_accepted_and_the_word_reaches_the_caller` also passed: no reading was accepted and the error names `acceptance_criteria`.

criteria.criterion: A unit test shows a `behavior` criterion, out_of_scope, title and defaults_applied text holding a boundary word are accepted; `cargo test -p athena-core` passes.
criteria.evidence: I ran it and it passed. A table puts the word into each of these fields: title, out_of_scope[0], defaults_applied[0], departures, hard_reason, urgent_reason, a criterion switched to Behavior, and assumptions[0]. Every case must be Ok, and any Err panics with the field named. A question and a decline_reason are each tested as separate readings and are accepted.

findings.summary: Two changed files are not on the expected deliverables list: crates/athena-core/src/run_pin_tests.rs and crates/athena-core/tests/refusal_corpus.rs.
findings.evidence: The diff stat shows changes to both files, and the deliverables list has only reading.rs, decisions.md and CHANGELOG.md. Both files are in the critic-accepted demonstration plan and contain only test changes. The end-to-end test in run_pin_tests.rs asserted the old summary refusal and would have failed without the change; refusal_corpus.rs holds the criterion 4 demonstration. findings.summary: After this change, nothing scans the title, summary or criterion text before it reaches landing commit messages and the PR title.
findings.evidence: D153 states this openly and proposes a follow-up: sanitize the text at those sinks with `plain_boundary_text`. The request asked to drop the summary and title scan, so this follows the request. It is still a real gap the user should decide on.

findings.summary: One rewrapped doc line in the `check_reading_acceptance` doc comment is longer than the surrounding wrap width.
findings.evidence: The line ending "...against the files at the base commit ([`check_boundary_and_repo_files`]; `repo_files` is `None` when" runs past the roughly 120-column wrap the other lines use. rustfmt does not reflow comments, so fmt still passes.

summary: The change does what the request asks: a boundary word in a reading's prose is no longer refused, and a word in a deliverable path or a `content` acceptance criterion still is. In code, `check_boundary_and_repo_files` now scans only deliverable paths and `content` criteria, through `file_bound_text_fields`. The new tests check both directions. I ran them and they pass: the prose-accepted test, the path/content-refused test, the unscanned-fields table, both end-to-end run_pin_tests and the refusal corpus. The policy test also passes. fmt, clippy and the full suite passed in Athena's recorded CI run. The module docs, the function docs, D153 and the CHANGELOG entry give the reason (records are outside the policy scan; the writer runs the scan, D73), the alternatives considered, and the refusal counts stated by the request. All criteria are met. There are two minor findings: two planned test files changed outside the deliverables list, and the gap D153 discloses, where title, summary and criterion text now reach commit messages and the PR title with no scan.
